description: Ten actual preview-observed screen studies. No live interaction, current mobile responsive rendering, usability or efficacy assumed; external images are linked, not redistributed.

cases.title: RCA Records — curated music & releases
cases.creator: RCA Records / Awwwards published design
cases.observed: The accessible image shows a dark canvas with a very prominent CURATED BY RCA section label, horizontally aligned bordered artist/article cards, human portraits, tiny neon-green category markers, short titles with underlined destinations, small circular back/forward controls, and a second FEATURED PLAYLISTS row. Media cover cards are treated as editorial units rather than identical administrative tiles.
cases.mechanism: Strong categorical editorial framing and recognizable artist imagery distinguish content types while maintaining individual click targets. A clear second row provides an alternative browsing rhythm.
cases.risks: Preview alone does not establish accessible carousel controls, screen-reader or keyboard behavior, responsive crop, or whether a user can find a track quickly. Horizontal cards could obscure items on a narrow device.
cases.original_exercise: Design one Night story with a featured recording, supporting fan photographs, and an explicit See all link; compare staggered editorial scale against an equal-card grid at 390px. Preserve artist approval and actual target links.
cases.source_claim: Awwwards hosts a specific RCA Records website-design gallery; image reflects a historical captured design.
cases.not_copy: RCA logo, artist photos, label trade dress, colors/type treatment.
cases.observation_limits: Single image crop only; no browser interaction, current live site or mobile state examined.

cases.title: Wax Poetics — music magazine editorial system
cases.creator: Wonderland / Wax Poetics
cases.observed: A large black condensed COSMIC REVERB heading shares a paper-colored magazine grid with spacious serif article text, a black-and-white crop of a musician to one side, a bright warm image sliver at the far edge, slim lines dividing columns and tiny dates/bylines. Each article feels like an authored page, not a uniform component card.
cases.mechanism: Typographic hierarchy, strong photographic subjects, purposeful asymmetry, and large unused space give each story distinctive weight while recurring labels preserve editorial continuity.
cases.risks: Magazine-style fine print and asymmetric cutoffs may fail on small screens. The project's portfolio image is not evidence of a functioning mobile reading journey.
cases.original_exercise: Build a Night Recap issue cover followed by one substantial feature story, supporting moments and precise event credit. Ensure long artist names and true edit/share actions remain clearly navigable.
cases.source_claim: Wonderland publishes this case study as its Wax Poetics design work; separate Awwwards historical site listing exists.
cases.not_copy: Wax Poetics masthead, original portrait photography, magazine identity, specific layout tracing.
cases.observation_limits: Studio screenshot crop. No live navigation, responsive reflow, text zoom, or keyboard interaction tested.

cases.title: A Foreigner's Guide to Polish Electronic Music
cases.creator: Culture.pl / Awwwards example
cases.observed: Large densely set black multi-line typography dominates a very pale left content field, with a compact introductory paragraph and circled Enter Article affordance below. A highly saturated magenta and blue cropped cultural image occupies a far-right field, separated by generous empty white space around the copy.
cases.mechanism: A bold article thesis anchors attention while the cultural image provides a counterweight; a modest clear action creates an entry point into a long-form story.
cases.risks: Display headlines may be hard to reflow at 320px, and a small outlined entry control could have an inadequate touch target. Historical cultural content cannot become generic neon-electronic branding.
cases.original_exercise: Compare a massive editorial headline plus one contextual concert image with an image-led Night hero using the same verified band, venue, date and CTA. Measure small-screen legibility.
cases.source_claim: Awwwards labels this specific work as a Culture.pl visual design reference.
cases.not_copy: Illustration, color treatment, branded article composition or typography specifics.
cases.observation_limits: One desktop-sized screenshot crop, no verified interaction, current state or mobile rendering.

cases.title: HEM Records — contemporary music player / identity
cases.creator: Dine / HEM Records
cases.observed: The design studio image shows a spacious light desktop music visual with vertical image/color strips and thin graphic geometry. Alongside it sits a narrow black phone-shaped treatment with a tinted translucent record image, visible Menu text, the track name Shallower Drum & Bass, a secondary musician credit, a pause control and NOW PLAYING display words at the bottom.
cases.mechanism: The music/media object stays expressive while minimal, recognizable playback controls form a distinct lower-contrast utility layer. Desktop exploration and mobile listening have different visual density but share a graphic voice.
cases.risks: Image does not prove playback really works, that the mobile view is fully responsive, or that small controls meet touch targets. Complex animated compositions may be costly on older GPUs.
cases.original_exercise: Use an artist-approved hero visual and a calm functional track card with a visible play/pause state and music credit, keeping a separate route for editing/linking media.
cases.source_claim: Dine hosts an HEM Records identity and digital-work case study.
cases.not_copy: HEM logo, sleeve art, music, track asset, exact visual identity.
cases.observation_limits: One studio composite, not a real user session, device recording or measured performance test.

cases.title: Lady Gaga — artist-first digital home
cases.creator: Yung Studio / Lady Gaga
cases.observed: A large subdued artist portrait dominates the center and right, with a pale decorative marginal field on the left. Three crisp horizontal action banners sit over the photograph, colored black, white and strong vermilion. The banners contain specific commercial/drop/presale messages with compact close controls; the person remains the visual and emotional context.
cases.mechanism: Artist identity can be primary without hiding important actionable campaign messages; layered calls to action need careful hierarchy and explicit priority.
cases.risks: Multiple overlapping promotional banners compete and may obscure the artist's face or content on mobile. Studio-stated traffic and sales are self-reported and cannot be treated as transferable UX effectiveness. Image rights and fan consent matter.
cases.original_exercise: Make an artist headquarters hero with a single verified fan action and a subordinate event/share action. Compare one CTA with three offers at 390px and with media blocked.
cases.source_claim: Yung Studio presents the Lady Gaga website project; the 2026 Webby winners list names a Gaga artist site.
cases.not_copy: Artist likeness, iconography, specific campaigns, proprietary hero artwork, brand name.
cases.observation_limits: Studio promotional image only; no current live interaction/browser/keyboard testing.

cases.title: Mobbin — finding app patterns by screen and flow
cases.creator: Mobbin
cases.preview_source: Third-party published image of Mobbin research UI
cases.observed: The screenshot shows a white research page headed Find design patterns in seconds, with a compact pill navigation, a tab row for Screens, UI Elements, Flows and Text in Screenshot, and horizontally arranged phone preview cards grouped by screen problem including Home, Subscription & Paywall and Login.
cases.mechanism: Search and classification by task/component are more reusable than a large unstructured moodboard. Explicit result type (screens versus flows) prevents overstating what an image proves.
cases.risks: An illustration of Mobbin's site does not grant paid-library access or prove the existence of a particular product screen. Third-party preview might differ from the 2026 live product.
cases.original_exercise: Build a local reference search that returns few grounded hits, labels link-only vs preview-observed vs interaction-tested, then lets the designer open the real source.
cases.source_claim: Mobbin's public website describes shipped screens, application flows and element search.
cases.not_copy: Mobbin screenshots, its classification UI, paid app captures or private data.
cases.observation_limits: Third-party screenshot preview, not authenticated Mobbin account or flow interaction.

cases.title: Tiptap — rich-text collaborative editing
cases.creator: Tiptap
cases.observed: A dark toolbar carries compact heading/list/code/quote controls in a single row over a pale document area. Horizontal grey text blocks illustrate a document, with visible color-coded collaborator cursors and name tags for You, Jane and Devon. The page shows a functional editing metaphor but the text is illustrative skeleton content.
cases.mechanism: Contextual editing operations and named cursor presence can be visually distinct from content; core writing canvas remains quiet. Collaboration state should be explicit rather than inferred.
cases.risks: The source screenshot does not demonstrate reliable autosave, persistence, collaboration latency or screen-reader interaction. A true collaborative editor is substantially more complex than a toolbar.
cases.original_exercise: Build a single-author Night Story inline editor with save/error/draft states; introduce collaboration only if genuinely needed and supported. Keep typography readable when the keyboard opens.
cases.source_claim: Tiptap's official product site documents a headless extension-based rich-text editor and collaborative options.
cases.not_copy: Tiptap logo, proprietary commercial extension screenshots or claims of implementation coverage.
cases.observation_limits: One official product illustration, not an actual editing session or keyboard test.

cases.title: Apple Photos — curated Memories card
cases.creator: Apple Photos / Apple Support
cases.preview_source: Apple Support screenshot from an older iOS guide
cases.observed: The cropped iPhone view shows For You and a Memories section with See All as a clear secondary destination. One large photograph-led Summer 2021 card dominates, with an overflow action and a heart at its top corner. The strongly colored picture gives the memory emotional prominence over the interface chrome.
cases.mechanism: A meaningful moment can be promoted as one curated story while the collection remains navigable through a distinct See All affordance. A small meaningful number of actions competes less with photography.
cases.risks: Old iOS interface may have changed substantially by 2026. The cropped preview does not establish the full playback experience, album management or privacy rules. A personal photo memory is different from a public concert gallery.
cases.original_exercise: Feature one actual Night's representative photograph and give access to all other Night galleries without relegating captions, privacy or editing actions to hidden gestures.
cases.source_claim: Apple support documentation describes Photos memories; this image is an older-version instructional screenshot.
cases.not_copy: Apple interface, private photo subjects or copyrighted image pixels.
cases.observation_limits: Cropped older mobile screenshot, no current Photos device session or gestures tested.

cases.title: Uppy Dashboard — selecting and inspecting uploads
cases.creator: Uppy / Transloadit
cases.observed: A large pale drop zone announces Drop files here, paste or import from and displays recognizable disk/cloud source icons. Below it, three selected file cards show media thumbnails, truncated filenames, file sizes, edit pencil icons and x removal affordances. A dashed border frames the active workspace.
cases.mechanism: Clearly separate source choice, staged files, per-item metadata/action and upload progress. The user can recognize what is queued before committing anything.
cases.risks: This is Uppy 0.8 from 2016: current Uppy Vue APIs and presentation differ. No upload progress, accessibility, drag/drop behavior or backend implementation is established from this picture.
cases.original_exercise: Create a calm media picker with Photos, Video and Audio source options, preview and title/caption, explicit audience and publish action, and truly supported progress/retry states.
cases.source_claim: Official Uppy historical release documents this screen; current Uppy Vue docs separately discuss headless and dashboard options.
cases.not_copy: Historical Uppy brand UI/screenshot; do not treat deprecated APIs as current.
cases.observation_limits: Old product screenshot only; current components must be checked against up-to-date Uppy Vue docs.

cases.title: Spotify — compact Now Playing mobile hierarchy
cases.creator: Spotify (screenshot republished by pi.fyi)
cases.preview_source: Third-party capture of Spotify player screen
cases.observed: A tall mobile composition with substantial colorful record artwork gives way to prominent song title and artist, a small green selection/check affordance, a horizontal playback progress line with current/total time, and a row of highly legible transport controls dominated by a large circular pause button. Auxiliary shuffle/repeat/output actions are smaller and flank the primary player.
cases.mechanism: Media/image and song identity are dominant, the current playback task has a clear central control, and secondary actions are present but visually subordinate. Control sizing reflects task frequency.
cases.risks: This third-party screenshot may be old or a custom rendering; we have not confirmed its exact app version or actual seek behavior, lyrics navigation, offline states or rights. Spotify trade dress and playback semantics must not be copied verbatim.
cases.original_exercise: Create an original embedded song/recording card for an artist Night with unmistakable play/pause/seek controls, correct licensing and clear distinction from an uploaded live recording.
cases.source_claim: Third-party page reproduces a Spotify playback screenshot; source is not Spotify's current official documentation.
cases.not_copy: Album artwork, Spotify logo/trade dress, exact player composition or copyrighted music.
cases.observation_limits: Third-party mobile screenshot only; no actual app interaction or date verified.
